understanding: The Stage-1 scaffold (src/oko/memory/scene.py: SceneModel/SceneStore/BackgroundPlate/SpatialGrid/FurnitureRegistry) is done and green (tests/test_scene_memory.py). The job now is to wire it into the live pipeline and then build the rest of a safe, autonomous per-camera continual-learning loop that fine-tunes YOLO on the user's own static-camera scenes. The immediate in-scope work is Chapter 2: update each camera's SceneModel every frame via SceneStore.get_or_create+save (plate/grid/furniture), and after a 2-5 min warmup SUPPRESS detections that match promoted furniture AND show ~0 motion vs the background plate so they neither wake the VLM nor raise a Telegram alert — the principled fix for the known chair/furniture false-trigger that also lets the conf threshold stay low for better recall. The static-track signal this needs already exists in events/builder.py (_static_track_ids, ratio<0.05 over 8 frames) and is currently thrown away per-event; SceneModel makes it durable, immediate, and cross-restart. Stages 2-5 (VLM/operator-validated label collection, held-out eval harness, YOLO dataset export, gated GPU fine-tune with auto-rollback + 1 Telegram confirm) are designed but each is a later, independently-shippable chapter. Everything is decomposed into 1-file atoms; verify == pytest in bridge-projects/oko; architect reviews each chapter's atoms.
summary: Build strictly chapter-by-chapter, Chapter 2 first, splitting each chapter so the LOGIC lives in pure, fully-unit-tested functions and the pipeline wiring stays thin. Chapter 2 = 5 atoms: (2.1) a pure scene-update function (downsample frame to the 16x12 grid, update plate only on non-moving cells, observe spatial grid + furniture), (2.2) a pure suppression predicate, (2.3) wire SceneStore observe-only into pipeline/live.py with throttled save, (2.4) wire warmup-gated suppression, (2.5) an opt-in config section default-off. Suppression requires BOTH a promoted-furniture class/IoU match AND ~0 plate-diff in the matched cells, is gated on a wall-clock warmup, and withholds BOTH the VLM call AND the alert through ONE explicit suppression decision point — the plate-diff is the safety backstop that lets any real person through because their pixels differ from the learned empty/furniture plate. Stages 2-5 follow as separate gated chapters, with the only model-changing stage (5) strictly last: training labels are YOLO's own VLM/operator-validated bboxes (not parsed VLM prose), GPU fine-tune runs out-of-band over runs/datasets, and promotion happens only on a held-out margin with no per-class recall regression, via atomic weight swap, retained previous weights for instant rollback, and a single Telegram confirm.

decision_atoms.statement: Build ONLY Chapter 2 (Stage-1 -> live integration) now; keep Stages 2-5 as reviewed design, each its own future chapter, with no code until Chapter 2 is merged and architect-reviewed.
decision_atoms.reason: AUTOTRAIN_PLAN.md states every stage is shippable on its own and the operator already approved Stage-1-first; on a high-risk task this avoids a big-bang and delivers the false-alert reduction immediately.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: User sees the actual YOLO-retrain payoff later, not in this increment.

decision_atoms.statement: Decompose Chapter 2 into 5 atoms with logic-as-pure-functions first: (2.1) pure scene_update fn, (2.2) pure suppression predicate, (2.3) wire SceneStore observe-only into live.py, (2.4) wire warmup-gated suppression, (2.5) config section.
decision_atoms.reason: 'Passes its own tests' is only honest if the logic is testable without a camera/pipeline; pure functions get exhaustive deterministic unit tests, and the two live.py atoms only need thin integration tests.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Two extra small modules (memory/scene_update.py, memory/scene_suppression.py) instead of inlining in live.py.

decision_atoms.statement: Suppression must withhold BOTH the VLM wake AND the alert ('не будить VLM, не слать тревогу'), implemented as ONE explicit suppression decision point in live.py that yields a suppressed PipelineEventResult (vlm_outcome should_query=False, reason='scene_normal_furniture', non-alerting bridge_output) — never scattered checks.
decision_atoms.reason: It is a literal task requirement, and a single auditable decision point is far easier to test and reason about than per-branch suppression.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires touching the result/reporter contract so a suppressed event is not dispatched as an alarm.

decision_atoms.statement: Require BOTH conditions to suppress — promoted-furniture class+IoU match AND ~0 plate-diff in the matched cells — and gate on warmup; the plate-diff is the safety backstop that passes a real person (still or moving) because their pixels differ from the learned empty/furniture plate.
decision_atoms.reason: Furniture-match alone would suppress a person occupying a chair's spot; the plate-diff is exactly the static-camera trick that makes suppression safe, and is the whole reason the background plate exists.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: A person who stands dead-still over a promoted bbox for the full promotion window is a residual blind spot.

decision_atoms.statement: Activate warmup on WALL-CLOCK elapsed (>= configured 120-300s from the first frame), not raw frame_count, while keeping frame_count for stats.
decision_atoms.reason: live.py explicitly notes the camera delivers uneven/bursty frames, so frame_count would cross the threshold too early or too late; '2-5 min' is a time spec.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Diverges slightly from the scaffold's frame_count-based is_ready; needs a small added time gate alongside it.

decision_atoms.statement: Source the furniture registry from the EXISTING static-track signal (events/builder _static_track_ids, which already targets static person/animal misdetections — the chair-as-person case); SceneModel only makes it durable, immediate, and cross-restart.
decision_atoms.reason: Plan note (c) says to persist exactly this signal that is currently thrown away per-event; it reuses proven logic and directly fixes the known chair false-trigger without inventing new detection code.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Behaviour is bound to that signal's window/ratio parameters (8 frames, ratio<0.05).

decision_atoms.statement: Stage-2 training labels = YOLO's OWN agreed bbox+class (the detection the VLM/operator confirms is real), NOT the VLM Russian free-text parsed into classes; furniture + confirmed-normal become hard negatives.
decision_atoms.reason: YOLO fine-tuning needs reliable class+box; parsing VLM prose into trustworthy labels is infeasible and unsafe, whereas the detector already supplies class+box and the VLM/operator only needs to act as a binary real/not-real validator.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Cannot learn brand-new classes from VLM text — only re-weight existing classes to these specific scenes.

decision_atoms.statement: Stage-5 GPU fine-tune runs OUT-OF-BAND (a separate CLI/scheduled job over runs/datasets), never in the live hot loop; promotion = atomic weights swap with a retained weights/prev copy + held-out gate + 1 Telegram confirm; rollback = restore prev.
decision_atoms.reason: Training is slow and GPU-heavy and must not stall live inference; an atomic swap plus retained previous weights gives instant, deterministic rollback.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds orchestration (job scheduling, weight-dir layout) outside the pipeline.

decision_atoms.statement: Make the promotion gate concrete: promote new weights ONLY if held-out beats current by a clear margin AND no per-class recall regresses beyond an epsilon; otherwise discard and keep current.
decision_atoms.reason: The 'never silently degrade' guarantee can be defeated by a single aggregate metric (e.g., mAP up while a critical class's recall drops); a per-class guard closes that hole.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: A stricter gate may reject marginal-but-genuine improvements.

decision_atoms.statement: verify == pytest in bridge-projects/oko for every atom, run green before the atom goes to architect review, and every chapter ships only after its full atom set is green.
decision_atoms.reason: It is an explicit task constraint and matches the success_tests; it keeps each 1-file change independently provable.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: None material beyond the discipline of writing tests per atom.

assumptions: A LivePipeline instance handles a single static camera (per _select_camera); multi-camera is handled by repeating get_or_create+save per camera_id on a shared SceneStore.
captured.image is a decoded image array available each frame inside LivePipeline.run(), so the 16x12 plate downsample and plate-diff can be computed directly from it without new capture plumbing.
Detections expose pixel-space bbox + class_name + confidence, normalizable by frame.width/height for furniture IoU and spatial-grid cell assignment.
'2-5 min warmup' means ~120-300s wall-clock; default 180s, configurable.
The Stage-1 scaffold (scene.py API + green test_scene_memory.py) is the agreed, stable surface and will not be reshaped under this work.

The existing stack (Ultralytics YOLO + CUDA GPU + a VLM + Telegram outbound) is wired; Stage 5 reuses it, and Stage 2 additionally needs inbound Telegram (getUpdates/webhook) which does not yet exist.
Suppressed events still update SceneModel statistics (they are evidence the furniture persists); only the VLM call and the alert are withheld.

risks.risk: Suppressing a real, motionless person who happens to occupy a promoted-furniture bbox.
risks.mitigation: Require ~0 plate-diff in the matched cells (a person's pixels differ from the learned plate), set a high furniture promotion threshold, never suppress when cell plate-diff exceeds the threshold, and log every suppression with crop/bbox/cell for audit and replay.

risks.risk: Background-plate poisoning: EMA updates on frames that actually contain a slow or static person drift the 'empty' plate to include them.
risks.mitigation: Only update plate cells with no overlapping active non-static track, keep EMA alpha small, and run warmup unattended; reuse the existing static-track guard to mask moving content.

risks.risk: Over-suppression reduces recall exactly when the user wants MORE detection sensitivity.
risks.mitigation: Opt-in config flag default off, ship the observe-only atom (2.3) before the suppression atom (2.4), provide a per-camera kill switch, and emit suppressed-count metrics/logs for monitoring.

risks.risk: Scope creep / big-bang: attempting to land Stages 2-5 together on a high-risk task.
risks.mitigation: Strict chapter gating with architect review per chapter; the only model-changing stage (5) is built last and behind the held-out gate.

risks.risk: Silent model degradation after a retrain.
risks.mitigation: Freeze a held-out slice never trained on; promote only on a margin with no per-class recall regression; retain previous weights; auto-rollback; require a single Telegram confirm.

risks.risk: Per-frame scene update adds latency to the live loop at ~30 fps.
risks.mitigation: 16x12 grid ops are O(192) per frame and outside the VLM path; persistence is throttled (save_interval 30s); measure before/after rather than assume.

risks.risk: Persistence corruption if the process crashes mid-save.
risks.mitigation: Scaffold already writes to .tmp then atomic replace and load() falls back to fresh components on any read error; add a test asserting partial/corrupt files degrade to a fresh model rather than crashing.

minimal_version: Ship Chapter 2 only, observe-then-suppress, opt-in. Land atoms 2.1 (pure scene_update function + exhaustive unit tests), 2.3 (SceneStore wired observe-only into pipeline/live.py via get_or_create + throttled save, updating plate/grid/furniture each frame), and 2.5 (config flag, default off). This already delivers a durable per-camera SceneModel updated every frame with green pytest — satisfying the 'SceneModel updated on each frame via SceneStore.get_or_create+save' success test — WITHOUT yet changing any alert/VLM behaviour. It is the lowest-risk first increment; the suppression atoms (2.2 pure predicate + 2.4 warmup-gated wiring) follow once observe-only is reviewed and proven stable.
advanced_version: Complete Chapter 2 (all 5 atoms, including wall-clock-warmup-gated dual suppression with the plate-diff backstop, a single suppression decision point, and a suppression audit log), then proceed as sequential, independently-shippable chapters: Stage 2 — a VLM/operator-validated label store (crop + class + conf + cell + plate-diff + verdict) under runs/labels/<camera_id>/ plus the inbound Telegram 1-tap path; Stage 3 — a held-out eval harness that freezes a never-trained slice and reports precision/recall/confusion per camera and per class; Stage 4 — YOLO-format dataset export under runs/datasets/ with agreed detections as labels and furniture/confirmed-normal as hard negatives; Stage 5 — an out-of-band gated GPU fine-tune with an atomic weight swap, a margin + no-per-class-regression promotion gate against the Stage-3 held-out set, retained previous weights for instant auto-rollback, and a single Telegram 'keep the improvement?' confirm. Every chapter is its own pytest-gated atom set under architect review, and the only model-changing stage is strictly last.
